worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The private notice revised the incremental competitive benefit from 12 to 2 while leaving the expected alternative-regulation burden at 12. Under the competitive-advantage assessment, continued support yields 2 minus the proposal cost of 6, or -4. The coalition therefore decided not to support the proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition no longer supports the federal carbon-pricing proposal. Private commercial assessments underlying this decision remain confidential.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that confidential, dated records surrounding comparable notices will associate support changes with revisions to competitive benefits, while revisions confined to alternative-regulation burdens will usually leave support unchanged.
worlds.derivation: Under CA, the support payoff depends jointly on the incremental competitive benefit and the common proposal cost. The notice changes exactly one benefit, so only a notice revising the competitive benefit normally changes the decision threshold; the independent reversal error weakens but does not eliminate the predicted association.
worlds.extra_assumption: Researchers can identify the type and timing of private notices from sufficiently reliable confidential records.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: Yesterday's reliable notice lowered the expected burden of alternative regulation from 12 to 2. The incremental competitive benefit remains 12. Applying the competitive-advantage rule gives a net payoff of 6 after subtracting the proposal cost. The coalition decided to continue supporting the proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to endorse the federal carbon-pricing proposal. Confidential commercial estimates will not be released.
worlds.candidate_implication: Across a larger documentary series, internal decisions should be substantially more stable after notices concerning alternative-regulation burdens than after notices concerning incremental competitive benefits.
worlds.derivation: The notice categories are equally likely, but under CA only the competitive benefit enters the payoff. With the proposal cost fixed at 6, burden-only revisions do not alter the calculated payoff; decision reversals occur only with probability .05.
worlds.extra_assumption: The surviving documentary series is not selected according to whether support changed.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The private commercial notice reduced the incremental competitive benefit to 2; the expected burden from alternative regulation remains 12. Net support payoff is therefore -4 after the proposal cost. The coalition decided to withdraw support.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal. Its private commercial analysis remains undisclosed.
worlds.candidate_implication: Occasional contradictions between internal decision records and next-day public statements should appear without corresponding changes in the underlying commercial calculations.
worlds.derivation: Internal memos faithfully record actual decisions, whereas public notes independently report the opposite decision with probability .05. Therefore, some documentary pairs should disagree even when the internal calculation and decision are coherent.
worlds.extra_assumption: Researchers can link internal memos and public notes to the same coalition decision episode.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The reliable notice revised the expected alternative-regulation burden downward to 2 but left the incremental competitive benefit at 12. Under the competitive-advantage hypothesis, the relevant net payoff remains 12 minus 6, equal to 6. The coalition decided to maintain support.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition maintains its endorsement of the federal carbon-pricing proposal. No private commercial figures are being disclosed.
worlds.candidate_implication: Internal memoranda should discuss competitive positioning more consistently near final support decisions than public statements do, even when both documents report the same decision.
worlds.derivation: CA makes competitive benefit decisive, internal memos may contain reasoning, and public notes withhold private commercial numbers. Jointly, these premises predict a systematic difference in documentary detail across internal and public records.
worlds.extra_assumption: Document-preservation practices do not systematically remove internal discussions of competitive positioning.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The notice lowered the incremental competitive benefit from 12 to 2, with the alternative-regulation burden unchanged at 12. Continued support has a net payoff of -4 after the proposal cost. Despite that calculation, the coalition reversed the normally indicated choice and decided to continue supporting the proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal. Confidential commercial inputs are not available for public release.
worlds.candidate_implication: A sufficiently large archive should contain rare internal records in which the stated competitive calculation points against the decision actually taken, without those exceptions forming a stable policy pattern.
worlds.derivation: Under CA, a competitive benefit of 2 minus the cost of 6 implies nonsupport, but the coalition independently reverses the indicated decision with probability .05. Thus calculation-decision mismatches should be uncommon and unsystematic.
worlds.extra_assumption: Internal memoranda preserve both the relevant calculation and the actual decision.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The reliable private notice reduced the incremental competitive benefit to 2 and left the expected alternative-regulation burden at 12. Subtracting the proposal cost of 6 produces a support payoff of -4. The coalition decided not to support the proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition has withdrawn its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal. Its confidential commercial estimates remain private.
worlds.candidate_implication: When confidential documents reveal downward revisions large enough to place competitive benefits below proposal costs, subsequent internal decisions should usually record withdrawal rather than continued endorsement.
worlds.derivation: CA defines payoff as competitive benefit minus proposal cost, and the coalition normally follows the payoff's sign. The .05 reversal probability implies a strong probabilistic prediction rather than an exceptionless one.
worlds.extra_assumption: The documents report benefit and cost figures using comparable units.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The notice changed the expected burden of alternative regulation from 12 to 2, while the incremental competitive benefit stayed at 12. Because the competitive-advantage calculation remains 12 minus the proposal cost of 6, continued support yields 6. The coalition decided to retain its endorsement.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition remains in support of the federal carbon-pricing proposal. Private commercial calculations will remain confidential.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should find that substantial revisions to anticipated regulatory burdens sometimes receive attention in internal files without producing a corresponding change in the coalition's recorded position.
worlds.derivation: The notice can substantially revise the regulatory burden, but under CA that quantity does not enter the support payoff. With competitive benefit above cost, support therefore normally continues despite the burden revision.
worlds.extra_assumption: Internal records mention material burden revisions even when those revisions do not change the decision.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The private notice lowered the incremental competitive benefit from 12 to 2; the expected burden of alternative regulation remains 12. The net payoff from support is -4 after deducting the proposal cost of 6. The coalition decided to end its support.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition does not support the federal carbon-pricing proposal. The underlying commercial figures are confidential.
worlds.candidate_implication: In matched internal-public document pairs, public notes should disclose less about the numerical basis of decisions than internal memos, regardless of whether the public note accurately states the decision.
worlds.derivation: Private commercial numbers are withheld from the public, internal memos may contain reasoning, and public-note accuracy concerns the decision rather than disclosure of its numerical basis. These premises jointly predict an information gap across document types.
worlds.extra_assumption: Researchers obtain lawful access to both internal and public records.
